chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abu Abdullah al-Barqi, from one of our companions, who said:

A woman handed over to me some yarn and said, 'Hand it over at Makkah so that the covering of the Ka'bah may be sewn with it.' But I disliked handing it over to the guards, and I knew them. So when I arrived in Medina, I entered upon Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) and said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you! A woman gave me some yarn and instructed me to hand it over at Makkah so that the covering of the Ka'be may be sewn with it. But I disliked handing it over to the guards.' He said, 'Buy honey and saffron with it, and take clay from the grave of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), and knead it with rainwater, and put some of the honey and saffron in it, and distribute it among the Shias so that they may use it to heal their sick.'

key_terms.الْحَجَبَةِ: the guards or officials in charge of the Ka'bah
key_terms.طِينُ قَبْرِ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: clay from the grave of Abu Abdullah (Imam Husayn)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq advise regarding the yarn given for the Ka'bah?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the Shia principle of prioritizing direct, communal benefit over bureaucratic ritual, as Imam al-Sadiq (AS) redirects the yarn from the Ka'bah's official custards to a more impactful use. By mixing the purchased honey and saffron with clay from Imam Husayn’s grave and rainwater, the Imam establishes a spiritual and physical remedy for the sick, emphasizing the intercessory value of the Ahl al-Bayt’s remains. This practice underscores the Shia view that devotion is best expressed through tangible care for the community rather than mere adherence to institutional protocols.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Abu Abdullah Al barqy, from one of our companions who said,

‘A woman handed over some yarn to me and she said, ‘Hand it over at Makkah for the covering of the Kabah to be spun with it’. But, I dislike that I should hand it over to the guards (of the Kabah), and I knew them. So when I came to Al-Medina I went over to Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, so I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! A woman gave me some yarn and instructed me that I hand it over at Makkah for the covering of the Kabah to be spun with it. But I disliked to hand it over to the guards’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Buy some honey with it, and saffron, and take some clay from the grave of Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> (Imam Husayn<sup>asws</sup>), and knead it with water of the sky (rain), and make something from the honey and the saffron to be in it, and distribute it upon the Shias for them to heal their sick ones with it’.
en.sarwar: 5. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from abu ‘Abd Allah al-Barqiy from certain persons of our people who has said the following:

“Once, a woman gave to me a certain amount of yarn as gift to al-Ka‘bah to be used in stitching its covering. I disliked giving it to the caretakers because I knew them. When I arrived in al-Madinah I went to visit abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam. I said to him, ‘I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause, a woman gave to me a certain amount of yarn as gift to al-Ka‘bah to be used in stitching its covering and I disliked giving it to the caretakers.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Buy with it saffron and honey, then take a little of the soil from the grave of abu ‘Abd Allah, al-Husayn, ‘Alayhi al-Salam. Mix it with water from the sky, a certain amount of honey and saffron; then distribute it among the Shi`a so they can use it as curing medicine for their patients.’”
